old_wikitext: For decades, [[Wallachia]] had been under Ottoman control and had to obey the sultan. The Wallachian rulers acted as representatives of the Ottomans and were required to provide soldiers to support the Ottoman army. However, [[Principality of Transylvania (1570–1711)|Principality of Transylvania]] changed its policy and offered support, giving Wallachia a chance to fight against the Ottomans. In 1594, [[Michael the Brave]], Voivode of Wallachia, formed a secret alliance with [[Sigismund Báthory]], Prince of Transylvania to resist Ottoman rule. [[Aaron the Tyrant]], Voivode of Moldavia also joined the alliance, and Michael launched attacks on Ottoman strongholds along the Danube. [[Istanbul]] depended on Wallachia for food, and Michael's rebellion caused serious food shortages. In 1595, a 40,000-strong Ottoman army under the command of Grand Vizier [[Koca Sinan Pasha]] marched to suppress the Wallachian rebellion. Wallachia acknowledged Sigismund's suzerainty on May 20, followed by [[Moldavia]] on July 3.
